name: Carrigcleena
text: Carrigcleena names two large Irish rocks held sacred to Clidna. The Irish carraig Chliodhna reads plainly as Clidna's rock. This countryside belief endured into the late nineteenth century. The better-known stone, seven miles SSW of Mallow in County Cork, once seemed a door to the Otherworld. People said Clidna dwelt in a greensward set within a circle of stones. Her kindness would spare the district from blighted corn and diseased cattle. Mischievous spirits also kept away. A second stone, tied to Clidna as well, rests near the strand at Inch. This pebble lies two miles southeast of Ross Carbery in County Cork.
